register.source_checks: The issue says this repository's packing-witness verify at e6e8d577, run unmodified on the witness, reports VERIFIED (exact-algebraic, 20706 pairs), and that verifier/sqcheck.py, an exact checker the author's lab wrote separately from this repository's code, reports VALID (exact rational); it says the two share only the unit-square, wall and non-overlap definitions. The witness's claim block says coordinate_provenance: reported. No local-optimality, rigidity or formal check is claimed. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
register.credit: Credit Doğa Özden (https://dogaozden.com/math/live/square-packing/), who reports a packing started from the registry's 204, Evan Daniel's #845 certificate (T-257), whose lineage Daniel states starts at Daniil Ostashev's s(176) packing (#575): 24 squares move by more than 0.05, 14 are re-tilted by more than 1 degree (largest 25.6), and the tilted set has 76 squares against 79. The issue asks that the improvement be credited to Özden and the base packing to its holders as the record lists them. The search was AI-assisted, the checks were run by code that did not produce the packing, and the issue and repository were prepared and posted by Özden's AI agent, which uses the account kenaznia-doga; Özden directed the work. The Kaggle dataset kmmmvs/squares-in-squares-best-packings the issue cites holds 204 at 14.807627474, above this, and the Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard's side-only 14.803489183116 (Cats and boxes, 27 October 2026), which #845 quoted, states no packing and is no report.
register.next_rung: Independently review the retained replay and the certificate (stage 4): a clean-room exact checker, the identity against T-257's packing and the lineage the source states, a mapped review whose acceptance would raise both rungs. Then adopt it at 204 in place of T-257 under the house rule, with both strong generators' regularization and the flip of the new house in the same change.
